clesRetenues: Q Aisyah Noor (Morgan Stanley) - QuantiFERON vs QIAGEN growth comparison and quantification of destocking: management explains that Diasorin reports only CLIA results whereas QIAGEN includes ELISA, making the direct comparison invalid; destocking is acknowledged but not quantified, the analyst being invited to compute it themselves.

Q Aisyah Noor - instrument sales vs consumables: 80% of current placements are on agent rental, with instrument sales representing minimal revenue, attributed to customers' inability to predict their seasonal revenues.

Q Odysseas Manesiotis (BNP Paribas) - cost line movements and disclosure changes: three cost drivers detailed - wage increases (one third of the growth), NES launch investments exceeding 10 M EUR/yr (one third), normal inflation (the balance).
Q Odysseas Manesiotis - LIAISON NES platform differentiation: simplicity highlighted ('2 components vs 8', '17 minutes vs 40') compared with competitors, hands-free operation for local laboratories.

Q Kavya Deshpande (UBS) - guidance implications and margin sustainability: gross margins expected stable with EBITDA improvement via operating leverage, offset by molecular mix dilution and the deterioration in China, balanced by the benefits of the German plant closure.

Q Kavya Deshpande - clarification of the China impact: the China decline could reach 7 M EUR rather than the 5 M EUR previously guided, with VBP expansion and aggressive competitive pricing described as the driver.
Q Jan Koch (Deutsche Bank) - assumptions on the easing of the headwinds: quarterly progression already communicated showing a Q2 expected slightly positive against a negative Q1.
Q Jan Koch - LTG order timing effects: H1 2025 had shown +15% then H2 -14%, the current Q1 decline of -7% being tied to order patterns that should normalise in H2.
Q Jan Koch - NES investment timing: less than 2 M EUR of the 10 M EUR planned has been spent in Q1.

Q Anna Vaktis (BofA) - positioning within the guidance range (high vs low end): management declines to specify, says it is comfortable reaching the range, the Q2 results will bring more directional clarity.

Q Anna Vaktis - Middle East exposure and mitigation of the oil impact: 5 M EUR of confirmed annualised impact tied to the supply chain/raw material costs with oil >100$/barrel, excluded from guidance as not material in Q1.

Q Natalia Webster (RBC) - US immuno growth excluding weather and QuantiFERON: the underlying US business delivered in line with the previous quarters excluding weather effects, normalisation observed in March.
Q Natalia Webster - status of Europe volume normalisation: current growth 0,5%-2% per quarter against 6% historically, returning towards a normalised pre-COVID level of around 1,5%.

Q Natalia Webster - sustainability of the Middle East mitigation: Iran identified as a 3-4 M EUR exposure with distribution uncertainty, other regions mainly facing logistics challenges via the Dubai port disruptions.

Q Philip Omnu (JPMorgan) - D&A guidance under the NES launch: Alberto expects an increase in depreciation tied to NES instrument installations and to the amortisation of the GI panel intangibles from the following months onwards.
Q Philip Omnu - impact of the new competition on guidance: guidance does not incorporate competition from the Roche TB test expected at end-2026, no material competitive impact anticipated for 2026.

Q Aisyah Noor (Morgan Stanley) - how to reach ~27% Molecular growth in H2 given the weakness in H1, NES adoption signals: normalised flu season, LIAISON PLEX base absent last year, NES placements not yet material contributors to revenue.
Q Aisyah Noor - tariff refunds booked in Q2, remaining balance: 2,5 M EUR of refunds received in Q2, timing of the balance uncertain (H2 2026 or 2027).

Q David Westenberg (Piper Sandler) - Q3 momentum trends, confidence in easier flu comps and in the product launches: immunodiagnostics continued growth expected, Q1 destocking judged exceptional, molecular dependent on flu normalisation, LTG expected to deliver a 'mid-double-digit' performance.
Q David Westenberg - syndromic panel vs single-test mix and reimbursement changes: management declines a detailed answer, defers the discussion to Q4.

Q Ankit Verma (JPMorgan) - timing of the H2 tariff refund and annual FX guidance: ~2,5 M EUR received in Q2, balance 'no visibility', EUR/USD assumption of 1,15-1,16 implying ~25 M EUR of annual FX impact.
Q Ankit Verma - directional colour on NES placements: too early for precise figures, distributor feedback described as 'very good'.

Q Anna Ratcliffe (BofA) - is the QuantiFERON strength in Q2 a catch-up from the Q1 destocking or underlying momentum: 'not a catch-up', the Q1 destocking by the large private laboratories has normalised, volumes 'continue to increase' in the US.

Q Anna Ratcliffe - clarification of the LTG guidance (slides low-single-digit but commentary mid-to-high-single-digit): LTG could 'deliver a positive surprise', with instrument placements recovering faster than expected.

Q Charles Pitman-King (Barclays) - NES pricing strategy and economic visibility: refusal to disclose competitive pricing, 140 USD reimbursement noted for four-test respiratory panels with minimal denials.
Q Charles Pitman-King - were the H1 S&M cost savings one-off or operational: three factors - operating leverage, favourable LTG mix (+7%), tariff refund partly offsetting the tariff costs.

Q Odysseas Manesiotis (BNP Paribas) - LIAISON PLEX outpatient/inpatient mix and impact of the MolDX expansion: initial placements in private laboratories (100% outpatient), hospital mix 60-70% inpatient, MolDX concerns addressed via a mini-panel strategy aligned with reimbursement trends.
Q Odysseas Manesiotis - QuantiFERON opportunity in secondary markets and China expansion: China faced with 26 local ELISA suppliers, secondary-market opportunity via higher-throughput LIAISON kits.
Q Odysseas Manesiotis - confirmation of the PLEX customer count unchanged Q1-Q2: more than 150 customers, with Q2 including blood panel placements and activations in existing respiratory accounts.
Q Jan Koch (Deutsche Bank) - quantifying the LTG growth drivers (order timing vs life science recovery): effects not separable, recommends following the partners' commentary ('B2B business').
Q Jan Koch - progress of the GI panel launch and benefit from the current outbreak: only just launched, two accounts validated, 'no GI effect yet' in the Q2 figures.
Q Jan Koch - will the PLEX customer count be disclosed in future: more than 150 customers, with the focus shifting to installations and add-on modules.

Q Natalia Webster (RBC) - respiratory vs non-respiratory revenue mix expected for PLEX: respiratory remains >70% of the syndromic market, the 2026 guidance assumes respiratory at 'more than half' of revenues.
Q Natalia Webster - can the 6-12 month implementation lead times be shortened: timeline unchanged, validation/IT integration complexity requiring the usual 6-12 months.
Q Natalia Webster - Middle East inflation impact of 8-10 M EUR in the 2026 guidance: minimal impact to date, the reserve clause removed from guidance, to be reassessed for 2027.
Q Kavya Deshpande (UBS) - high-throughput QuantiFERON gross margin vs the standard version: 'exactly the same margin structure' as the previous version.
Q Kavya Deshpande - potential for converting the customer base to high throughput: conversion targeted at '100%', 30-35% already converted, completion expected by year-end.

pointsCles: Q2 26 revenue +4% cc (+5% ex-China and ex-molecular respiratory), exactly on the quarterly path laid out in March: Immunodiagnostics +4% (+5% ex-China; US back to double-digit historical growth on the hospital strategy, 600-hospital year-end target confirmed; Q1 QuantiFERON destocking and US weather effects behind; China ~-25% on VBP with no H2 improvement expected; Iran at zero revenue vs EUR 1.5M in Q2 25), Molecular +1% (+4% ex-respiratory; targeted specialty MDX +25%), LTG +7% (positive surprise, faster-than-expected Life Science recovery, now seen mid-to-high single digit FY).

H1 26 revenue EUR 602M flat cc (-3% reported, FX headwind -20M of which only -3M in Q2 vs -17M in Q1); adjusted EBITDA 194M (-7% cc), 32% margin with a marked sequential step-up from 31% in Q1 to 33% in Q2 (operating leverage demonstrated, ~EUR 3M/quarter tariff impact absorbed); adjusted EBIT 149M (-10% cc, 25% margin, reported EBIT 125M); IFRS net profit 84M (-15%), adjusted net profit 106M (-16%); Q2 revenue 315M with net profit flat at 46M.

Balance sheet deliberately stretched by capital returns: net debt EUR -844M at 30/06 (vs -580M end-2025, -265M swing) after 233M of buyback outflows and 65M of dividends, partly offset by positive but lower H1 FCF of 58M (vs 83M, deliberate NES-launch inventory build); the EUR 250M buyback is ~95% executed (~3.6M shares, ~6.5% of capital, 236M) and H2 cash generation is expected to improve on stronger earnings and inventory normalization.

LIAISON NES commercial via distributors since April but still zero disclosed numbers ('too early', placements typically land right before the season; second 510(k) - Group A Strep - completes the panel; first quantification promised for Q3/Q4); LIAISON PLEX now above 150 customers (90% hospitals, ~2/3 of placements in flex configuration), blood panel launched and GI panel just approved (2 accounts validated, fast-expanding funnel), full-panel Europe launch planned Q1 27, activation timelines unchanged at 6-12 months; US reimbursement of ~$140-142 per 4-target mini-panel with minimal denials validates the mini-panel strategy, with Roche and bioMerieux themselves moving to smaller panels.

hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
H1 2026 came in flat at constant FX exactly on the quarterly path management laid out in March (Q1 -3%, Q2 +4%), earning a second integral reaffirmation of FY26 guidance (revenue +5/+6% cc, adjusted EBITDA margin 32-33%). The major event of this refresh is a margin-driven correction: H1 EBIT of 149M on the Omnium base forced a rebuild of FY26 EBIT to ~300M (vs 215M at setup, +40%) - carried through the whole 2026-2030 trajectory. LIAISON PLEX traction is now real (150+ clients, GI panel just launched); LIAISON NES is commercial but still without a single disclosed number.

== THESIS READ ==
- Credibility signal: the quarterly progression matched the plan twice - supporting the H2 acceleration (molecular ramp) the guidance requires. Watch: Q3 molecular print.
- The +40% EBIT correction is extrapolated from H1 margin holding, not from explicit guidance at that granularity - medium confidence by construction. Watch: H2 margin confirmation.
- NES is the key unpriced optionality, two quarters into commercialization without numbers. Watch: first NES disclosure.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Omnium base reintegrates the recurring Luminex acquired-intangible amortization (~35-40M/yr) that Diasorin excludes from its 'adjusted' metrics (rule E5e) - hence Omnium EBIT sits structurally below management figures. Buyback nearly complete (shares 52 -> 49M). No reliable sell-side consensus (basis null). Iran/Middle-East exposure bounded.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
FY26 bottom-up: H1 EBIT actual 149M + H2 at held margin -> ~300M. 2027-2030: scale factors from the 2026 correction (EBIT x1.395, Net x1.381) applied to the Investor-Day plan (revenue CAGR 6-8%, adjusted EBITDA margin 34-35% by 2030). Bridge: ETR 25%, finNet -15 to -11M with deleveraging (net debt 750 -> 60M); published 2025 reconciles at zero residual. Watch: EUR/USD (guidance assumes 1.18); QuantiFERON restocking; net-debt bump from the buyback.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 results (Nov); first NES quantification; PLEX GI panel ramp; FY27 guidance (Mar 2027).

ancrages.moteur: MAJOR REVISION at this refresh: the creation model (09/07/2026), based on Q1 26 alone (adjusted EBIT -17% cc), implied an FY2026 EBIT of around 215 M EUR (margin ~17%). Actual H1 26 shows adjusted EBIT of 149 M EUR on a margin of 24% cc/25% at current rates - well above the creation assumption. Bottom-up reconstruction retained: actual H1 (EBIT 149 M EUR) + H2 estimated by broadly holding the H1 margin (management flags no expected deterioration, only a revenue acceleration driven by NES/PLEX in full season), giving an FY2026 EBIT of ~300-310 M EUR (retained at 300 M EUR out of prudence, the H2 trajectory remaining partly an extrapolation).

FY2026 guidance (revenue +5%-6% cc, EBITDA margin 32%-33%) reaffirmed without any change for the 2nd consecutive time (after Q1 and then Q2), despite an H1 flat at constant currency - management explicitly states that it remains confident given the expected normalisation of the Q1 base effects (flu, QuantiFERON destocking, weather) and the NES/PLEX ramp-up in H2.

Management explicitly confirms that around +27% organic growth is required in H2 in Molecular to reach the annual 'low double-digit' target, explained by an almost nil comparison base on PLEX/NES in H2 2025 (products not yet launched) rather than by a heroic assumption on underlying organic growth - execution risk to be monitored but a build mechanism judged credible by management itself.

LIAISON NES still has no sales figure disclosed by management ('too early', 'not significant') - second consecutive quarter without quantifiable traction. The full panel is now available (2nd Group A strep test cleared under 510(k)), real commercial visibility is expected at the Q3/Q4 calls with the flu season - a major point of friction with the market (Deutsche Bank note of 15 June, NES 2030 potential estimated at 97-126 M EUR against 125-200 M EUR implied in the group guidance) remains unresolved.

250 M EUR share buyback programme ~95% executed at the time of the call (236 M EUR, ~6,5% of the share capital, ~3,6M shares) - diluted share count revised slightly lower vs creation (49M for 2026 against 50M), the dilution from financing this programme (increased net debt) already being incorporated in omniumND.

Net financial position deteriorated to -844 M EUR at 30/06/2026 (against -580 M EUR at end-2025) under the combined effect of the buyback programme (233 M EUR) and dividends (65 M EUR), partly offset by a positive but declining H1 FCF (58 M EUR vs 83 M EUR, tied to the NES inventory build) - 2026 deleveraging trajectory revised, the net debt peak now confirmed higher than the creation assumption.

Iran exposure confirmed close to zero in Q2 26 (against 1,5 M EUR of revenue in Q2 25, an effect expected to persist over the remainder of 2026 according to the CFO) - an isolated and bounded impact, consistent with the 3-4 M EUR annual estimate retained at creation, with no extension identified beyond it.

rupture.motif: Les indicateurs ajustés du S1 2025 ont été retraités par l'émetteur (note (*) du communiqué du 31/07/2026) pour réallouer sur l'ensemble de 2025 les coûts opérationnels de la filiale chinoise, initialement comptabilisés en totalité au T4 2025. Le comparatif S1 2025 n'est donc plus celui publié en juillet 2025 : aucun CAGR ni aucune variation semestrielle ne traverse ce point sans drapeau.
